claims.text: The starting material is an equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr blend containing metallic powders and TaH0.5, NbH, HfH2, TiH2, and ZrH2.
The precursor has an initial oxygen content of approximately 500-1000 ppm.
Mixed-powder additive manufacturing can drive in-situ alloy formation in a refractory high-entropy alloy.

The proposed treatment consists of a 2 degrees Celsius per minute ramp to 800 degrees Celsius, a 2-hour hold, rapid heating to 1250 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes, and immediate water quenching at more than 100 degrees Celsius per second.
ZrH2 decomposition generates an in-situ reactive zirconium getter atmosphere.
The zirconium getter maintains oxygen partial pressure below 10^-15 atm throughout hydride decomposition.
The dual-stage treatment produces sequential decomposition and complete dehydrogenation of all precursor hydrides.
Hydrogen released by hydride decomposition creates a reducing environment.
Localized hydride decomposition creates a transient liquid phase at decomposition interfaces.
Transient liquid-phase sintering promotes densification and refines the grains to the sub-micron or near-micron scale.
Zirconium scavenges residual oxygen through the reaction Zr + O2 to ZrO2 and suppresses oxygen uptake by the alloy.
Lowering oxygen activity below a critical threshold prevents thermodynamic stabilization and nucleation of an alpha-HCP phase.
Oxygen contamination affects phase formation in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Rapid quenching bypasses a diffusion-controlled alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC transformation and traps the high-temperature beta-BCC phase.
The getter-assisted process yields a nearly fully dense alloy with relative density greater than 98%.
After quenching, the alloy is a metastable single-phase beta-BCC material.
The quenched grain size is 0.5-2.0 micrometers.
The getter-treated and quenched alloy contains no alpha-HCP or alpha-Ti precipitates.
Sintering without a getter typically produces alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC or alpha-HCP plus beta-BCC, oxygen-induced embrittlement, and grains larger than 5 micrometers.
The proposed outcome requires sufficient getter capacity and fails if getter exhaustion or overly slow heating lets oxygen ingress outpace scavenging.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that success requires pO2 below 10^-15 atm, whereas the experiment only declares falsification when pO2 remains above 10^-14 atm. The intermediate range from 10^-15 to 10^-14 atm is therefore inconsistent with the stated success condition but is not classified as a failure.

The hypothesis confidently attributes sub-micron refinement to transient liquid-phase sintering, while the uncertainty field says transient liquid formation is uncertain and might instead cause excessive grain growth.
